question_text: Why was everyone scared of breaking the news to Mrs. Mallard?
stimulus_text:
Knowing that Mrs. Mallard was afflicted with a heart trouble, great care was taken to break to her as gently as possible the news of her husband's death.

It was her sister Josephine who told her, in broken sentences; veiled hints that revealed in half concealing. Her husband's friend Richards was there, too, near her. It was he who had been in the newspaper office when intelligence of the railroad disaster was received, with Brently Mallard's name leading the list of "killed." He had only taken the time to assure himself of its truth by a second telegram, and had hastened to forestall any less careful, less tender friend in bearing the sad message.

She did not hear the story as many women have heard the same, with a paralysed inability to accept its significance. She wept at once, with sudden, wild abandonment, in her sister's arms. When the storm of grief had spent itself she went away to her room alone. She would have no one follow her.

There stood, facing the open window, a comfortable, roomy armchair. Into this she sank, pressed down by a physical exhaustion that haunted her body and seemed to reach into her soul.

She could see in the open square before her house the tops of trees that were all aquiver with the new spring life. The delicious breath of rain was in the air. In the street below a peddler was crying his wares. The notes of a distant song which some one was singing reached her faintly, and countless sparrows were twittering in the eaves.

There were patches of blue sky showing here and there through the clouds that had met and piled one above the other in the west facing her window. She sat with her head thrown back upon the cushion of the chair, quite motionless, except when a sob came up into her throat and shook her, as a child who has cried itself to sleep continues to sob in its dreams.

She was young, with a fair, calm face, whose lines bespoke repression and even a certain strength. But now there was a dull stare in her eyes, whose gaze was fixed away off yonder on one of those patches of blue sky. It was not a glance of reflection, but rather indicated a suspension of intelligent thought.

There was something coming to her and she was waiting for it, fearfully. What was it? She did not know; it was too subtle and elusive to name. But she felt it, creeping out of the sky, reaching toward her through the sounds, the scents, the color that filled the air.

Now her bosom rose and fell tumultuously. She was beginning to recognize this thing that was approaching to possess her, and she was striving to beat it back with her will - as powerless as her two white slender hands would have been.
stimulus_ref: Story appreciation set 10 (The Story of an Hour part 1: the news), pp476-477
answer_text: Everyone was scared because Mrs. Mallard had a heart condition, and the news might harm her health.

question_text: Why do you think Mrs. Mallard felt happy and free?
stimulus_text:
When Mrs. Mallard abandoned herself a little whispered word escaped her slightly parted lips. She said it over and over under her breath: "free, free, free!" The vacant stare and the look of terror that had followed it went from her eyes. They stayed keen and bright. Her pulses beat fast, and the coursing blood warmed and relaxed every inch of her body.

She did not stop to ask if it were or were not a monstrous joy that held her. A clear and exalted perception enabled her to dismiss the suggestion as trivial.

She knew that she would weep again when she saw the kind, tender hands folded in death; the face that had never looked save with love upon her, fixed and gray and dead. But she saw beyond that bitter moment a long procession of years to come that would belong to her absolutely. And she opened and spread her arms out to them in welcome.

There would be no one to live for during those coming years; she would live for herself. There would be no powerful will bending hers in that blind persistence with which men and women believe they have a right to impose a private will upon a fellow-creature. A kind intention or a cruel intention made the act seem no less a crime as she looked upon it in that brief moment of illumination.

And yet she had loved him - sometimes. Often she had not. What did it matter! What could love, the unsolved mystery, count for in face of this possession of self-assertion which she suddenly recognized as the strongest impulse of her being!

"Free! Body and soul free!" she kept whispering.

Josephine was kneeling before the closed door with her lips to the keyhole, imploring for admission. "Louise, open the door! I beg, open the door - you will make yourself ill. What are you doing Louise? For heaven's sake open the door."

"Go away. I am not making myself ill." No; she was drinking in a very elixir of life through that open window.

Her fancy was running riot along those days ahead of her. Spring days, and summer days, and all sorts of days that would be her own. She breathed a quick prayer that life might be long. It was only yesterday she had thought with a shudder that life might be long.

She arose at length and opened the door to her sister's importunities. There was a feverish triumph in her eyes, and she carried herself unwittingly like a goddess of Victory. She clasped her sister's waist, and together they descended the stairs. Richards stood waiting for them at the bottom.

Someone was opening the front door with a latchkey. It was Brently Mallard who entered, a little travel-stained, composedly carrying his grip-sack and umbrella. He had been far from the scene of accident, and did not even know there had been one. He stood amazed at Josephine's piercing cry; at Richards' quick motion to screen him from the view of his wife.

But Richards was too late.

When the doctors came they said she had died of heart disease - of joy that kills.
stimulus_ref: Story appreciation set 11 (The Story of an Hour part 2: freedom and death), pp478-479
answer_text: She felt happy and free because she realized she could live her life for herself without any constraints of marriage.

Josephine was kneeling before the closed door with her lips to the keyhole, imploring for admission. "Louise, open the door! I beg, open the door - you will make yourself ill. What are you doing Louise? For heaven's sake open the door."

But Richards was too late.

When the doctors came they said she had died of heart disease - of joy that kills.

Mugdho's Sacrifice to Establish Rightful Demand
From the very young age, Mugdho always spoke up against injustice. So, when he saw the students fighting against the fascist Hasina government for their rightful demand of quota reform, he could not sit idle in the house.
On 18 July 2024, Mugdho set out to distribute food and water to the protestors who took part in the anti-discrimination students movement. He came out with water bottles and boxes of biscuits in hands. He shouted, "Water, water, who needs water?" He did so believing that the protesters were fighting for justice. Suddenly, law enforcers opened fire to disperse the crowd, and a bullet struck his forehead, exiting through his right ear. Doctors declared him dead upon arrival at Crescent Hospital. His selfless act of service, captured in a video just minutes before his death. Ultimately this tragic incident became a poignant symbol of the student-led uprising, highlighting the struggle for justice and change in Bangladesh.
Mugdho was honored as a martyr, with various tributes. It includes the renaming of a public space in his memory and the distribution of "Mugdho" water bottles at protests. His sacrifice continues to inspire activists until the fall of a fascist government.

Arif and an old woman

Hearing the life story Arif became very upset and called her father. Arif's father was a police officer and he came to the spot and took the woman to an old care center and assured the old-home officials that he will cover the expenses whenever needed. Arif had no grandma and he became very happy to call the woman as his grandma. In every occasion Arif and his family went to that old-home to see the woman and pass some time with her.

Once there lived a King in an island. There were green trees everywhere in the island. The King decided to build a magnificent palace in the island. So he ordered his men to cut down all the trees. Some opposed the King's idea but he did not pay heed to their opposition.
So people were compelled to carry out the king's order. They cut down all the trees. As a result, a great change to place in the climate of the island and the atmosphere rapidly turned hostile. The temperature increased rapidly. Extreme heat of the suns made soil crack. It eventually led to draught. Other disaster also started to visit the island. People could not grow crops. So there broke out a famine. As a result, many people had to starve to death. Others became rickety and pale.
At these the king realized his misdeed. He ordered his people to plant plenty of trees in the entire island. He felt repent for his wrong doing. But it was too late. It took to a long time to reinstall everything in proper order.

A Lucky Rickshaw Puller
Rahmat Mia is a poor rickshaw puller in Dhaka. He pulls rickshaw in different areas of the city. One day he saw some men selling lottery tickets. He felt tempted and bought a ticket. He knew the date of the draw. He was waiting eagerly for the day. Then the much awaited day came and he purchased a daily newspaper and went to his slum, to check his number on the sly. He was very excited as dream peeped into his heart unconsciously. He took out his ticket from a torn bag agilely. First he checked his own number and then looked on the paper to find his number out. To his utter surprise he found his number at the first prize place. He revised, revised and revised. But he could not believe his own eyes. What a surprise! He is the winner of the first prize that means he is the owner of 50 lakh taka. He thought to himself. He felt shouting but he did not do so. He told noting to anyone even to his wife; He on the sly communicated with the concerned authorities and got the money within a short time. In the mean time, his name was published in the newspaper as the first prize winner of the lottery. He told his slummates to spend a good portion for the welfare of them. He deposited half of the amount in a bank and with the another half he bought a land and built house there. He also gave his slummates some loans so that they might start a co-operative business. He himself also joined the business and their slums became a solvent one. Thus a lottery changes the fate of some slum dwellers.

Promise Should be Kept
A long time ago, the town of Hamelin faced with a great problem. It became full of rats. The situation became very unbearable.
The rats were so big and fierce that they fought the dogs, killed the cat and bit the babies in the cradles. They ate the corn in the granaries. They squealed all the time.
At last the people came to the Town Hall and said to the Mayor "Do something about the rats or we will send you packing." The Mayor trembled. He called a meeting of his councilors and talked about the problem for hours. But they could not find a way out. They were in despair. At that moment a pied piper came and went up to the council table and said, "People call me pied piper. If you pay me a thousand guilders, I will rid your town of rats." "All right," said the Mayor. "We'll pay you a thousand guilders. When will you set to work? "Now" replied the pied piper.
The pied piper went to the street, drew out a pipe from his pocket and began to play on it. Soon from every house in Hamelin came out the rats tumbling. There were hundreds and thousands of them that followed him. He went down to the bank of the river Weser and waded into the river. And every single rat, which followed him, was drowned. But the Mayor refused to pay the contracted money. At this the pied piper got angry and played on his pipe in another tune. Hearing the strange tune the children came out of their houses dancing and followed him. The pied piper disappeared behind a hill with all the children and did never come back.

The crow was in a fix what to do. Reasonably he became very disappointed. He was thinking what could be done. But he could not find any means to quench his thirst. At last, losing heart when he was about to fly away, he saw some pieces of stones lying at a little distance. At once he hit upon (মাথায় আসা) a plan. He got to the stones and took a piece of stone in his mouth. He flew to the pitcher and dropped the stone into it. He continued the same task for several times and gradually the level of water was rising.

Slow and Steady Wins the Race
There lived a hare and a tortoise in the same jungle. The hare used to taunt the tortoise for its slow pace. One day he challenged the tortoise in a race. The tortoise said, "You can run quite fast, no doubt. But I think you boast about your speed more than you can run. I think I can beat you."
"Do you hear that?" said the hare to a fox, who was standing near. "Could anyone even think that such a slow-coach could beat me in a race?"
"It would be a good joke if he did," said the fox. "Do you wish to run a race? I will be the judge, if you care to have me."
"That suits me well," answered the hare.
"I am willing," said the tortoise.
So the fox marked off a place for starting, and set up stake at the goal. The race began. The hare bounded along and was very soon far ahead of the tortoise. He called back to the fox, "I think I shall take a little nap before I finish the race; the tortoise will not reach here for an hour or more." So he lay down in some bushes and went to sleep.
Every minute brought the tortoise a little nearer to the goal. He did not stop for a second.
At last he passed the hare, but the hare still slept. On and on he plodded; it was a long way, but he had no thought of stopping.
He came nearer and nearer the goal. At last his foot touched the stake.
The hare wakened, stretched himself, and leaped toward the goal. "What, you here!" he cried when he saw the tortoise. "How did you ever reach here?"
"Just by keeping at it," said the tortoise.

The Fox and the Crow
One day a crow stole a piece of meat. It flew away and sat on the branch of a tree. Suddenly a fox came along and stopped under the tree. He sniffed something good to eat. Looking about, he saw the meat in the crow's mouth and wanted it.
How could he get the meat? He could not climb the tree. What good would it do if he could? The crow would fly away when she saw him coming. He could not coax the crow to come down to the ground. She knew what a fox likes to eat.
At last the fox had a happy thought. He said to himself, "A crow is one of the proudest birds I ever knew, I will flatter her and she will forget about the meat."
So he called out in his sweetest voice, "Good day, my pretty bird"; but the crow did not reply. She only stepped about proudly on the branch.
"I wish I had such a beautiful form as you have," said the fox.
Still no answer, but the crow held up her head and turned it first to one side and then to the other, showing that she was pleased.
"What a graceful neck and bright eye!" said the fox. "The other birds may well be jealous of you."
No answer yet. She only raised her wings a little and gazed down upon the fox.
"If your voice were only as beautiful as your form and your dress, you would be queen of all the birds; but it seems that you cannot talk at all. What a pity that you are dumb!"
The crow gave a loud "caw!" As she did so, the meat fell from her mouth. The fox snapped it up quickly. The poor crow at last understood that the fox was only fooling her but it was too late.

A Greedy Farmer
There lived a farmer in a village. He had a wonderful goose. The goose laid an egg of gold everyday. The farmer was very greedy (লোভী). He thought that, the goose laid only one egg a day. So it would take time for him to be rich. He thought if he cut the goose, he would get all the eggs at a time. And by this way he would be rich overnight (রাতারাতি). So he told his plan to his wife. His wife was a wise woman and she was not greedy. So she requested her husband not to do so. But the farmer did not listen to his wife. Finally he cut its stomach (পাকস্থলি) with a sharp knife. But alas! There was no egg in it.
The farmer was sorry. His wife also scolded him. She said, "You are foolish but greedy. So you have lost all."
Moral : Grasp all, lose all.

Even a Small Creature Can Help a Large one/ One good act deserves another
Once a lion was sleeping in a forest. Suddenly a mouse came there. It did not notice the sleeping lion. It was running about and playing happily. By chance it ran over the face of the lion. It awoke the lion. At this the lion grew very angry and caught the mouse. Then the mouse prayed meekly (নরম স্বরে), "Please let me go. One day you may need my help." The lion laughed and thought. "How could a little mouse help a lion?" Then he said, "Well, I will let you go but you must walk carefully." The lion set the mouse free.
The mouse was grateful. He thanked the lion. One day the mouse was looking for something edible. Suddenly he saw that the lion was caught in a net in the jungle. The mouse remembered the lion's assistance and started cutting the net with his sharp (ধারালো) teeth. Finally the mouse cut the net and set the lion free. The lion was also grateful to the little creature (প্রাণী). So he thanked the mouse and offered him to be his friend.

An Intelligent Boy
One sunny morning a boy of eleven years was tending cattle by the side of a railway line. Suddenly he noticed that a small railway slipper was about to collapse. A little while later, he remembered that a mail train was supposed to cross in about half an hour. He remembered (স্মরণ করা) the story of his grandfather. His grandfather once told him "We should show red cloths to the driver if the train is in dangerous position anytime." Then he put off his shirt. His shirt's colour was red. He tried to move the shirt in the air. He tried to catch the attention of the driver. It was unbelievable (অবিশ্বাস্য) that suddenly the driver could identify the boy's red shirt and thought about danger. The driver stopped the train. The driver got down from the train and found the damage of the rail line. The driver and all the passengers became astonished for the heroism (বীরত্ব) of little boy.

Accursed Child Labour
A poor girl, named Rina, worked in a rich man's house. The house master was kind to her but the mistress was very cruel (নিষ্ঠুর). She used to scold her now and then. One day while serving tea, Rina broke a cup of tea. The house mistress flew into a rage supposing it a great loss, and she made a spud hot and touched it to her arms and back. Moreover, crying was strictly prohibited (নিষিদ্ধ হওয়া) as there were some relatives present in their house. The house mistress made Rina clear the floor instantly. Rina felt nervous as she was little enough to do household chores.
However, she again entered the kitchen to make another cup of tea. Making it she began to move on to the guest room. But in the half way she stumbled and fell in the floor and the result became the same. Now catching Rina's disheveled (এলোমেলো) hair the mistress started beating her black and blue. She dragged her into the kitchen and locked the kitchen door leaving her inside.
The result went to a fatalistic end. Disgusted (বিরক্ত) with life, Rina cut her throat with a sharp knife that was in the kitchen.

The Brave Boy
One day some boys were playing cricket in a school ground. All on a sudden they heard a hue and cry (হৈচৈ) nearby. The boys stopped playing then and there and went to the spot. They found smoke coming out of a house. They rushed to the house and found a house on fire. There was nobody else near the fire. Only a few women were running to and fro. They were crying bitterly. The boys thought that there might be somebody in the house who could not come out. There were flames and flames on all sides. It was a great danger. The boys were too brave to cope with the situation. They were witty as well. One of them was really heroic. He then and there ran into the burning house.
The boy found an old woman there. She was too weak to move. The boy took her on his shoulders (কাঁধ). He then came out running with her. Other boys were shouting and trying to extinguish (নেভানো) the fire by throwing water. In the meantime, people from nearby houses and areas gathered there. People were, at bottom, amused to see this. They called them brave boys. The Headmaster of the school heard the story the following day. He congratulated the boys on their heroic (বীরত্বপূর্ণ) feat.
This was really a worthy act of which the school also felt proud.

Rescuing a Drowning Boy
Last Saturday I went to the river for taking my bath at 9.00 a.m. I saw two boys bathing in the river. Suddenly one boy fell into the deep water and cried for help. I rushed to the spot without making any delay. But by the time I reached the spot, the boy went under water and disappeared (বিলীন হওয়া). I was at a loss what to do. I said to the other boy, "Does he know how to swim?" the boy said, "No, he doesn't." I became very afraid realizing that the boy was drowning. I dived into the river and tried to rescue (উদ্ধার করা) the boy. But I couldn't trace the boy under the water. I dived several times and looked for him. After about one minute I could trace him and pulled him above the water. Very quickly I took him to the bank. The boy was then fully unconscious. I knew the first-aid of a drowned man. I gave him first-aid. After a while he got back his consciousness (চেতনা). By this time many ones gathered there. The parents of the boy were also informed of the incident. They rushed to the spot. They said to me, "You have saved our son's life. So we have been indebted (ঋণী হওয়া) to you." I said, "Don't say so, it's everyone's duty to save one's life". Then I left the place.

Fortune Smiles upon the Diligent
Once there lived a middle-aged woman named Bilkis. She had three sons. Her husband was very lazy and he did not do any work. None but she had to work all day long to earn money for the family. One day she met a group of people who came to her village from the Grameen Bank. They said they were interested in helping the poor people, the landless (ভূমিহীন) and the helpless. She learnt from them that only the poor and landless people were eligible (যোগ্য) ones to take a loan from the bank.
However, before they could borrow (ঋণ) money, they would have to make 5–6 groups of workers. Bilkis immediately started to look for people. Soon the necessary groups were formed. All the group members became registered members of the Grameen Bank project. Bilkis's group elected a Chairperson. The group Chairperson would be responsible (দায়ী) for discipline in the group. Members would conduct (পরিচালনা করা) their business with the bank through her. They were fully aware of the rules and procedures (প্রক্রিয়া) governing the activities of the group. In this process Bilkis got a loan of three thousand taka. She invested the amount in a small business. She repaid the loan money and got a bigger loan. In this way she became self reliant (আত্মনির্ভরশীল).
Eventually, all her family members started living happily with solvency.

Laziness Begets Failure
Jamal is an S.S.C examinee. He is not attentive to his lesson especially to English because he is very weak in English. Moreover, he is lazy. So his preparation in English is not good. A month ago before his examination he managed a short suggestion on English.
The examination was drawing near and he began cramming more and more. The appointed (নির্দিষ্ট) day of English exam appeared. With a heavy tremor all through the body Jamal entered the hall. Obtaining question paper in hand he got puzzled (হতভম্ব) as there were a few questions common in the paper. With a trembling hand he began to write through an over writing tendency and habit. He delivered inaccurate answer to his known questions even in the brunt of his heavy excitement. Final bell rang with the end of the fixed three hours of exam. Jamal left the hall leaving many questions unanswered. The result after three months was out and he was absent in the gazette.
Afterwards he became clear of his failure in English. Finally he understood his fault (দোষ) in study process. He took an oath (শপথ গ্রহণ) never to do such again in life.

A Dutiful Boy
Once a school boy named Ahsanullah was going home after completing his class. When he was crossing the road, he saw an old woman lying on the road. She was senseless (অচেতন). There was nobody to help her. Ahsanullah at once became concerned with the woman. He came to know that she had a collision (সংঘর্ষ) with a baby taxi. He took the wounded and unconscious woman to the nearby hospital in assistance with a rickshaw puller. The hospital authorities could not recognise the woman as Ahsanullah did not know her. Ahsanullah became her custodian and took the charge of her treatment cost. The woman came to life again. After some days she was fully cured (আরোগ্য লাভ করা). Now the question 'where the woman will go' was posed on. The woman replied that she would go to the home of Nabiullah. Ahsanullah became a little agitated and asked where Nabiullah's home was. 'Muradnagar' the reply was. "My village" Ahsan thought to himself. "Nabiullah, my father and in this village there is only one Nabiullah." The mystery became clear that the woman was Ahsan's father's only sister who never met her brother after her marriage. Ahsan warmly received her aunt and took her to his home with a happy heart.

A True Love Shown by Cordelia Towards her Father King Lear
Long long ago there lived a king in England. He was over eighty and in the wrong side of life. He had three daughters. He decided to divide his kingdom (রাজ্য) among his three daughters, but before doing that he thought of calling each of them to know how much they loved him. The eldest daughter told that she loved the king from the core of her heart. She loved him like honey. The second daughter told him that she loved the king like sweets. She could do anything for her father. At this the king was very glad and satisfied (সন্তুষ্ট). At last, he called his youngest daughter, Cordelia. The king wanted to know how much she loved him. Then the youngest daughter told that she loved him like salt. At this, the king became very angry.
He ordered his soldier to put her away in the jungle. The king divided the kingdom into two parts and presented equally among the two daughters. On the other hand, one day the prince of another country came for hunting into the jungle and found the youngest daughter of the king. The daughter was very beautiful and the prince liked her very much. He married her. After many years, the king was very helpless because his daughters left him away as they were very selfish (স্বার্থপর). Then the king left his kingdom and went to the jungle. One day he was very hungry and saw a palace nearby. He entered the palace and begged food from them. The youngest daughter came out and knew her father. She was very pleased to see her father and cooked many delicious (সুস্বাদু) food items. But she did not use salt and so the king could not eat the food. He rebuked (তিরস্কার করা) his daughter for not using salt. He told that he could not eat any food without salt. The daughter reminded him that she loved him like salt and so she was left away in the jungle. At this, the king became very sad and burst into tears. Then the king repented to his youngest daughter and prayed to God for her betterment.

Happiness Lies in the Contentment
Once there lived a happy cobbler who passed his days in working and singing from morning till night. A rich neighbor of his was banker who one day said to him, "How much do you earn a year?" The cobbler replied that he had never saved his one year's income and even he did not know how many days a year had. Hearing this, the banker became surprised (অবাক). He asked the cobbler what he did with his money. The cobbler told that he lived from hand to mouth. In fact the cobbler (মুচি) earned very little and spent all the money he earned a day to support himself and he had no ambition (আকাঙ্ক্ষা). He had no demand for amenities that had not possessed.
So poverty could not stand in the way of his happiness. At this, a deep thought occurred in the mind of the banker. He sighed, "How helpless I am!" A vast property belonged to the banker. But an unsatisfaction (অসন্তুষ্টি) always troubled him. So he always wanted more riches which snatched away his happiness. The banker said to himself, "What is use of this possession when I'm deprived of real peace?" He thought he was poorer than the cobbler. So he began to find out happiness giving away all his riches to the poor. In fact happiness is a relative factor which varies from person to person. It can't be possessed in spite of having vast properties.

Reporter : Asif, thank you for speaking with me today. I know this is a painful time, but can you tell us what happened when Abu Sayed was shot during the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement?
Asif : Thank you. It's hard to talk about. We were peacefully protesting, demanding a fair, merit-based system. But suddenly, the police showed up and tried to disperse us aggressively.
Reporter : I understand. What happened next?
Asif : The situation escalated quickly. Abu Sayed was standing beside me, chanting and holding a sign, completely unarmed. He was determined, but peaceful, like the rest of us. Then, a group of policemen started moving toward us. They didn't warn us; they just came closer with weapons ready.
Reporter : So, they opened fire without warning?
Asif : Yes, without any warning. I saw one of the officers aimed his gun at Abu Sayed and fired from a close distance. It was horrifying, inhuman. Sayed fell immediately—there was nothing we could do. It all happened so fast.
Reporter : That must have been devastating. How did the crowd react?
Asif : People were in shock. Some screamed, others tried to run.
Reporter : I'm so sorry for your loss. Why do you think this incident has sparked such an intense reaction from people across the country?
Asif : Because Abu Sayed's death wasn't just an attack on him—it was an attack on our right to speak, to demand a fairer society.
Reporter : Thank you, Asif.
Asif : Thank you too.

Fardin : I'm fine. And you?
Robin : Me too. Do you know what dengue fever is and what its parameters are these days?
Fardin : Yes, I know about it but not sure about my information.
Robin : Don't worry, let me clarify it to you.
Fardin : Sure.
Robin : Dengue is a kind of disease which spreads due to mosquitoes mainly Aedes Aegypti.
Fardin : Thanks for giving me this information. Can you tell me about the symptoms of dengue fever?
Robin : Sure. Actually high fever, vomiting, severe headache, severe joint and muscle pain, low blood pressure, weakness, skin rash are some of its symptoms.
Fardin : It seems a very dangerous disease.
Robin : Yes, it is a very dangerous disease. All the year round people are attacked by this disease.
Fardin : Can you tell me how we can get rid of dengue fever?
Robin : By taking rest and repose, drinking plenty of fluids and taking advice from doctor.
Fardin : Well, how can we prevent Aedes mosquito?
Robin : By destroying the breeding places of Aedes mosquito like old tyres, cans, flower pots having rainwater, keeping environment neat and clean, spraying insecticides and raising public awareness.
Fardin : Thanks.
Robin : Welcome.

Kajal : Yes, there is no alternative to it.

answer_text:
Anti-discrimination Students Movement
The Anti-discrimination Students Movement is a significant event in the history of Bangladesh. This movement starts demanding for fair treatment in the civil service quata system in Bangladesh. This movement ultimately turns into an epoch-making mass uprising against autocratic Hasina regime. The movement initiated by a group of student activists in Bangladesh in 2024. It emerged as students felt that the existing quota system was unjust. The movement gained momentum through organized protests, including marches, human chains, and blockades across various cities. A pivotal moment came when a student leader, Abu Sayed, was tragically shot by police. It galvanized support and intensified the protests. On August 5, 2024, the movement played a crucial role in a large uprising that led to the fall of the former fascist Prime Minster, Sheikh Hasina. This marked a significant change in the country's political landscape. Following this, some of the key members of the movement were appointed to advisory positions in the interim government, highlighting their rising influence. As they continue to advocate for reforms, there are plans to establish a political party to further their goals. The movement symbolizes the power of youth activisim in shaping Bangladesh's democracy.

answer_text:
The July Revolution-2024
The July Revolution of 2024 in Bangladesh marked a turning point in the nation's history. Initially sparked by students protesting the longstanding quota system, the movement soon became a powerful wave against the authoritarian rule, systemic corruption, that had built up over 16 years. The government, criticized for its deeply corrupt institutions and lack of accountability, responded with violent repression. In the early stage of the quota reform protests, the government's heavy-handed approach led to multiple student deaths, including those of Abu Sayed and Mugdha, and several others. This brutality ignited widespread outrage, and thousands took to the streets, transforming the student-led protest into a nationwide movement. Throughout the revolution, over a thousand students and citizens, including at least 67 children, lost their lives. By August 5, the people of Bangladesh had reached their limit and took to the streets in overwhelming numbers to oust the fascist regime. Being frightened, the fascist Prime Minister, along with family and close party members, fled the country, seeking shelter in neighbouring country, India. Following their departure, Nobel Laureate Dr. Muhammad Yunus answered the call of the people, assuming the role of Chief Advisor to an Interim Government on August 8. This revolution stands as a testament to the power of collective will. However, the July Revolution reshaped Bangladesh's political landscape, ushering in a renewed commitment to democratic principles and a hopeful future led by the voice of the people.
question_text: Write a Paragraph about "The July Revolution-2024".

The person who works in the farm lands for growing various agricultural products is called a farmer. Usually he lives in a village. He is a very important and useful person in the country. He grows and provides food for the people of our country. He is called the father of food production. But they are heavily devaluated. He gets up from bed early in the morning and takes a pair of bullocks and plough to cultivate his land. He works all day long in his land. In Bangladesh, farmers lead a very miserable life. If he can produce good crops, his face beams with joy. On the contrary, if he fails to grow, his sorrows know no bounds. Most farmers of our country live under poverty level. They live from hand to mouth. Bangladesh is mainly an agricultural country. Her prosperity depends on the development of agriculture. That is why, I cannot think of her without a farmer. Therefore, the farmer's prevalent condition ought to be upgraded to help his life reach a standard level.

answer_text:
Our National Flag (আমাদের জাতীয় পতাকা)
The national flag of Bangladesh is a symbol of pride and identity for the people of the country. It features a deep green background with a large red disc in the centre, representing the rising sun. The color green symbolizes the country's lush vegetation and agricultural heritage, while the red disc represents the bloodshed and sacrifices made during the struggle for independence from Pakistan in 1971. The flag has a rectangular shape with a length to width ratio of 10:6. The size of the national flag is regulated by law, with specifications for the proportions and dimensions of the flag for different occasions and uses. The flag is flown on public and private buildings, during national holidays and events, and on official government vehicles. The flag is also an essential component of the country's diplomatic representation abroad, and it is prominently displayed at Bangladeshi embassies and high commissions worldwide. The national flag is kept half-mast on the occasion of national mourning day and on the 21st February. However, our national flag is not just a piece of cloth, but it represents the identity and dignity of the nation. The flag serves as a unifying force that brings the people of Bangladesh together under a common goal of progress, development, and prosperity. The national flag of Bangladesh is a powerful symbol of the country's past, present, and future, and it inspires a sense of patriotism and national pride in the hearts of its citizens.
question_text: Write a paragraph on "Our National Flag." [RB '24, '23; JB '19; CB '16; SB '24; MB '24]

answer_text:
A School Magazine (বিদ্যালয় সাময়িকী)
A school magazine is an important part of any educational institution. It is a publication that is created by students and teachers alike and showcases the achievements, ideas, and creativity of the school community. A school magazine typically contains a range of content, from news and current events to features on the school's sports teams, clubs, and extracurricular activities. It may also feature interviews with teachers, students, and community members, as well as artwork, poetry, and short stories. In addition to providing an outlet for students' creativity, a school magazine can also help to foster a sense of community within the school. It allows students to learn about and appreciate the diverse talents and interests of their peers, and to celebrate their collective achievements. Publishing a school magazine is a valuable learning experience for students, as it requires collaboration, research, writing, editing, and design skills. Students who participate in the creation of the magazine gain valuable experience in journalism, publishing, and media production, which can be useful for them in their future academic and professional endeavours. Overall, a school magazine is an important part of the school community, providing a forum for students to express themselves, showcase their talents, and celebrate their accomplishments. It is a testament to the creativity, diversity, and academic excellence of the school, and an enduring record of the memories and experiences shared by its students.
question_text: Write a paragraph on "A School Magazine". [RB '19, '14; JB '24, '16, '14; SB '16]

answer_text:
Environment Pollution (পরিবেশ দূষণ)
Environment refers to the air, water, land in which people, animals and plants live. So human beings, animals, plants, air, water, soil etc are the main elements of the environment. The natural forces such as storms, cyclones and earth quakes are also a part of this environment. Environmental pollution means polluting the elements of the environment. Nowadays environment pollution is a burning issue. It is a global problem. It has become a tremendous problem also in Bangladesh. The environmentalists of our country express their great apprehension about our future environment and its effects. The people of our country are destroying our valuable forests day by day. The environment of our country is being polluted for want of sufficient forest resource. Unplanned massive industrialization is another cause of environment pollution. Smoke coming out from the mills and factories is polluting air. Smoke coming out from motor vehicles also pollutes air. Again, the waste products of the mills and factories are thrown into water, which causes pollution of water. The insecticides used in the fields of crops also pollute our environment. Environment pollution is gradually and dangerously changing the climate of our country. Many serious diseases are being caused by this. We must be conscious of the matter and try to get rid of this problem soon. The government should take all possible steps in order to improve this condition.
question_text: Write a paragraph on "Environment Pollution" in 250 words : [SB '16; DjB '19; CB '24]

answer_text:
A Tea Stall (চায়ের দোকান)
A tea stall is an ever-present and essential part of daily life. This humble roadside establishment is where people gather to catch up with friends, engage in discussions, and take a break from the hustle and bustle of daily life. The tea stall is typically a simple structure, consisting of a few wooden benches or plastic chairs, a small counter, and a large saucepan/cauldron of boiling water and a saucepan of milk for making tea. Customers can enjoy a hot cup of tea with a variety of snacks like biscuits, samosas, or singaras. The tea stall is a great equalizer, where people from all avenues of life come together to share a moment of relaxation. It is not uncommon to see students, office workers, shopkeepers, and even rickshaw pullers taking a break at the tea stall. The atmosphere is usually lively, with the sound of clinking glasses and chatter filling the air. In the evening, tea stalls transform into social hubs, where people gather to discuss politics, sports, and current affairs. A tea stall is not just a place to drink tea, it is a cultural phenomenon that reflects the warmth and hospitality of the people of our country. For many, a tea stall is a daily ritual, a place to unwind, and a respite from the chaos of the outside world. Whether you are a local or a tourist, a visit to a tea stall is a must-do experience that will leave you with a newfound appreciation for the simple pleasures of life.
question_text: Suppose, one day you visited a tea stall in your locality. You stayed there for about an hour and had some experiences about the stall. Now, write a paragraph on "A Tea Stall". [DB '15; CtgB '20; BB '24]

answer_text:
A Winter Morning (একটি শীতের সকাল)
A winter morning is a truly unique experience. Unlike other seasons, when the morning air is often warm and humid, a winter morning brings with it a crisp, refreshing chill that can invigorate the senses. The sun, still low in the sky, casts a warm golden glow over the landscape, and the early morning mist adds a dreamy quality to the scenery. The leaves on the trees and the grass on the ground are covered in dew, sparkling like diamonds in the soft light. As the sun begins to rise, people emerge from their homes, bundled up in warm clothes, ready to start their day. In the rural areas, farmers start their day early, heading out to tend to their crops and livestock, while others set out to collect firewood or fetch water from nearby sources. Children can be seen playing outside, their breath visible in the cold air as they run around. In the cities, life is a bit more fast-paced, but the chill in the air is still noticeable. People hurry to work or school, bundled up in warm clothes. Vendors selling hot tea, pithas, and other snacks can be found on street corners, providing some warmth and comfort to passerby. Shopkeepers open their stores, setting out warm clothes, blankets, and heaters for sale. Despite the cold weather, there is a sense of joy and excitement in the air, as people enjoy different types of pithas, date juice, etc. However, not everyone enjoys the winter morning. The poor suffer the most due to lack of proper shelter and warm clothes. Overall, a winter morning in Bangladesh is a mixed bag of emotions. It is a beautiful and serene time for some, while it brings about suffering and hardship for others.
question_text: Write a paragraph on 'A Winter Morning'. [CB '14; BB '23; DjB '24, '23, '15, '14]

answer_text:
Rohingya Exodus (রোহিঙ্গাদের দেশান্তর)
The Rohingya are minority community living in Rakhine State, Myanmar. There were around 1 million Rohingya living in Myanmar before the 2016-'17 crisis. On 22 October 2017, according to the United Nations, around 603,000 refugees from Rakhine, Myanmar had crossed the border into Bangladesh since August 25, 2017. This number increased to 624,000 by November 2, 2017 and over 625,000 by December 6, 2017. Besides, almost everyday more Rohingya people are entering Bangladesh. This is really a huge exodus of Rohingyas from Myanmar to Bangladesh. The majority of them are Muslim while the minority of them are Hindu. They are one of the most persecuted minority communities in the world. The Rohingya people are denied citizenship under the 1982 Myanmar Nationality Law. They are restricted from freedom of movement, state education and civil service jobs. They are deprived of basic rights and privileges. Genocide took place in Rakhine State. Many Rohingya people were beaten and burned to death. Many women were raped. Their houses were burned to ashes. So, they were bound to leave Myanmar and take shelter in Bangladesh and other neighbouring countries. They set up temporary camps in different areas of Cox's Bazar. The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh came forward to help the helpless Rohingya people. Besides, other countries came forward to provide them with basic things. They also donate the government of Bangladesh to help the distressed Rohingya people. The government of Bangladesh is trying to raise an international awareness to get a permanent solution to the Rohingya crisis. It is because the long term stay of the Rohingya people in Bangladesh will put heavy pressure on her economy.
question_text: Write a paragraph in 250 words on "Rohingya Exodus".

answer_text:
Online Education Programme Or, Digital Class
Online education programme is such an education system in which learners can receive education anywhere, anytime by using internet. Since the spread of COVID-19 pandemic, the tradition of online classes has accelerated to a great extent throughout the world. Almost all the countries of the world are conducting online education programme by using the online media like youtube, facebook, zoom, google meet etc. Bangladesh does not lag behind in imparting online education. Here the learners are getting interested in receiving education through online school because they need not attend classes physically. Through online classes both the teachers and students can see and hear one another. The learners can question their teachers and get answers. They can be highly benefitted from attending online classes. As they do not need to attend their academic centres, they can save their time and money. They do not need to prepare lecture sheets as they can save them in their respective computers or smart phones. Besides, they can protect themselves from pollutions, accidents, fatal diseases and pandemics like COVID-19. But there are some disadvantages of online classes. All the learners are not solvent. They are unable to purchase laptops or smartphones and internet package. So, we should take effective measures to make online schools successful.
question_text: Write a paragraph on "Online Education Programme" in 250 words.

answer_text:
A Road Accident
Road accidents are very common incidents in our country particularly (বিশেষ করে) in the city areas. To say, it happens frequently and regularly here and there in our surroundings. Recently, I have had an experience of witnessing such a serious road accident. The accident took place last week on the main Thana Sarak near our school, while I along with some of my friends was coming home from school. The road was not so busy at that time. Some buses and cars were plying usually. But all on a sudden there happened a crash in the twinkle of an eye. A bus losing control pushed a microbus plying aside and the microbus driver hit some passers-by who were walking along the foot path. One of them was run over by that microbus and was bleeding seriously in his head. The other two were also seriously injured. There raised a hue and cry. We, the students instantly decided to take the injured to the nearby hospital. We called a van and took them all to the hospital. We reached the hospital within half an hour. But the man who was bleeding in his head died after being taken to the doctor. I felt I could save them all by all my means. But I felt helpless and shocked. This shocking feelings are still hurting my heart.
[Words : 222]
question_text: Write a paragraph on "A Road Accident". [DB '20]

answer_text:
How to fight against Dengue Fever and face it
The dengue outbreak in the recent time has been very widespread in the major cities and towns of Bangladesh. People of all classes have been affected by this disease. This is a mosquito-borne viral disease. According to sources of various news agencies, about 20 thousand people have been attacked with this epidemic. At least 100 people died in different places. The problem has taken a strong shape in Dhaka city. Every day new dengue patients are getting admitted in the hospitals of Dhaka city. The government agencies and health workers are struggling hard to overcome the issue. All types of leaves of the doctors and other health workers have been cancelled. The government is trying its best to cope with the situation. They have also urged people to keep their areas clean and use all other familial measures by themselves. From our side, we should follow the paths of prevention. To face and remain safe from dengue fever, we must keep our homes, residence and the surrounding area clean. The houses should be free from all kinds of pots and bottles containing stagnant water for many days. All the members of the family must use net for sleeping both at day and night. Besides they can wear thick clothes and stocking both inside and outside of home. However, if anybody is attacked with dengue fever, he must take enough rest. He can also take paracetamol type tablet. And if the fever rises he must see a doctor. However, if we follow these preventive measures, we will be able to fight dengue fever and face it unitedly.
question_text: You are seen that 'Dengue Fever' is taking away a lot of lives from different districts in our country. Now, write a paragraph on "How to fight against it and face it". [RB '20]

answer_text:
Tree Plantation/ Importance of Trees
Tree plantation means planting more trees and plants. The purpose of tree plantation is to save the endangered (বিপদগ্রস্ত করা) environment and to beautify our life. Tree plantation is very important because it serves many useful purposes. We get flowers, fruits, fuel and timber from trees. Trees make air fresh and improve the environment. They save us from natural calamities like drought, storms, floods, etc. They increase the beauty of nature. They give us oxygen and take up carbon dioxide and thus maintain ecological (বাস্তুসংস্থানগত) balance. In absence of trees, the country will turn into a desert. So trees are a valuable asset for our existence. Among the seasons, rainy season is the best time for tree plantation. We can plant trees around our dwelling places and in open places. Moreover, trees can be planted by the roads, rivers, canals and playing fields. Awareness should be raised and campaign should be launched to motivate people for tree plantation. Thus we can make the tree plantation programme a success.
[Words : 164]
question_text: All the beings depend on trees for their existence. So we should plant trees more and more every year. Now. write a paragraph on "Tree Plantation". [RB '15; JB '20; SB '14; BB '15, '14]

answer_text:
Causes of Road Accidents in Bangladesh
At present road accidents are regular happenings in Bangladesh. Generally road accidents take place in the urban areas and in the highways. The causes of road accidents are reckless driving, brake failures of vehicles, over-taking of one vehicle by another, driving by unskilled (অদক্ষ) drivers. Over loading of vehicles is another reason for accidents. Another reason is violation (লঙ্ঘন) of traffic rules. Even the police cannot control the traffic rule breakers. Sometimes pedestrians (পথচারী) are crashed under the wheels of heavy vehicles. Sometimes the speedy vehicles fall into the roadside ditch or into the river and thus kill the passengers on the spot. Many lives are nipped in the bud. Many a family loses the only earning member. Many people become crippled. During the last vacation I met with an accident on my way to Rajshahi by bus. Luckily nobody was hurt. So road accident is like a curse in our life. This problem can be solved by all out efforts from both the authority and the general mass. To do so, first our general people have to be made aware. The drivers have to be skilled and they also have to avoid their overtaking tendency (প্রবণতা). And the authority should be more strict to enforce the rules. And these steps must be taken immediately to prevent road accidents.
[Words : 213]
question_text: Suppose, on the last vacation you were going to Rajshahi by bus. Unfortunately your bus met an accident but luckily there was no casualty or death. Now, write a paragraph on "Causes of Road Accidents in Bangladesh". [CB '20]

answer_text:
A Street Hawker
A man who sells various things by moving from street to street is a street hawker. He is a self-employed (স্বনিয়োজিত) person. He usually lives in a slum or in a house at a very low rent. He is a familiar (অতিপরিচিত) figure. He is seen almost everywhere in a village or in a town. He carries his materials on head and sometimes in hand and sometimes in a small handcart (হস্তচালিত গাড়ি). He earns his livelihood by selling cheap goods. He is a very cunning person. He buys goods at a cheaper rate and sells at a good profit. He sells toys, cosmetics, ready-made garments, utensils, sweets, ribbons, fruits, etc. He usually appears at noon or in the absence of the house master. He speaks in different ways, wears colourful dress and sometimes plays flute or raises high voice to draw the attention (মনোযোগ আকর্ষণ) of his customers. He walks for hours to sell his goods. Thus he passes his days by selling these goods. He gets up early in the morning and sorts his products for selling. He leads a very simple life. He has to toil a lot to earn his livelihood. He somehow manages his family with hardship. Even though he works hard and adopts (গ্রহণ করে) various tricks he leads a life below poverty line (দারিদ্র্যসীমা).
question_text: Write a paragraph on "A Street Hawker" within 150 words. [SB '20]

answer_text:
Water Pollution
Water pollution is the contamination (দূষণ) of water. No living being can pass a moment without water. Hence water is an essential element of nature. But polluted water is very harmful as it causes death threatening diseases like diarrhoea, cholera, jaundice, etc. It can be polluted in many ways. Man pollutes water by throwing waste materials into it. Using chemical fertilizers and insecticides (কীটনাশক) farmers pollute water. Rain and floods wash away these chemical fertilizers and insecticides to rivers, canals and ponds and thus water is polluted. Poisonous (বিষাক্ত) chemicals are used in mills and factories. Throwing their waste products into rivers and canals, they pollute water. Steamers, boats and launches throw oil, food and human waste into the water of rivers and canals. and thus make the water polluted. Because of this pollution, fish cannot survive. People also become ill by drinking and bathing in the polluted water. By checking the dumping of factory waste, water pollution can be minimized. We can also purify it by boiling or using purification (বিশুদ্ধকরণ) tablets. So, to keep good health, we must try to prevent water pollution.
flag_note: ছাপা নম্বরের প্রথম অঙ্ক পৃষ্ঠার কিনারায় কাটা বলে মনে হয় — শুধু '6.' দেখা যায়; নম্বর 16 ধারাবাহিকতা (13, 14, 15-র পর) থেকে ধরা হয়েছে।
question_text: Water is called life. But it is polluted in many ways. Now, write a paragraph in 250 words on "Water Pollution". [DjB '20]

answer_text:
The Bad Impacts of Deforestation
Deforestation means cutting and burning down of forests. There are many causes of deforestation. People are increasing like mice in a barn (গোলাঘরে ইঁদুরের বৃদ্ধির মতো). Their needs and necessities are also increasing. As trees and plants are of great use to them, they cut them down. They use timber to make furniture and firewood for fuel. By burning down forest, they also make living place. But they are not aware of the harmful effects of deforestation. Due to deforestation, carbon dioxide is increasing. And so the weather pattern is being changed. The world is becoming warmer. The heat of the sun is trapped (আটকা পড়া) inside the atmosphere. As a result, the polar ice caps are melting. And this situation will flood huge areas of the globe. As ours is a low-lying region, it may one day go under water. Therefore, effective measures should be taken to prevent deforestation. Tree plantation programme should be introduced. If one cuts down a tree, one should plant two trees. Besides, public awareness should be raised to grow more plants and trees.
[Words : 162]
question_text: Trees are the most important gift of nature. But cutting down trees affects our environment greatly. Now, write a paragraph in 250 words on "The Bad Impacts of deforestation". [MB '20]

answer_text:
My Visit to a Book Fair
A book fair is a special kind of fair where various kinds of books are displayed and sold. It gives an opportunity to buy different types of books at the same place. Recently I have visited a book fair at the Bangla Academy premises (চত্বর). Actually, it is an annual function and Bangla Academy authorities arrange the fair in memory of the language martyrs. It is termed "Amor Ekushey Boi Mela." When I entered the mela premises, I was really pleased at the calm and quiet environment. Though it was brimming (কানায় কানায় পূর্ণ) with people, there was no chaotic situation (বিশৃঙ্খল অবস্থা). I saw book lovers humming in the stalls without any trouble. I bought some books of varied interests. According to my list I collected some valuable books without any hazard. The decoration of the premises also pleased me very much. I was really fortunate as I met some eminent (প্রখ্যাত) writers of our country and I took autographs from them. Actually, I was really pleased at the fair and I hope it will uphold our culture in the arena of world literature (বিশ্ব সাহিত্য).
question_text: Write a paragraph on "Your Visit to a Book Fair". [DB '19; JB '17; CB '17, '15]

answer_text:
A Traffic Jam I Experienced
Bangladesh is a populous country. About 140 million people live here. A lot of vehicles is needed for a lot of people. That is why, a traffic jam is a very common scene in Bangladesh. Last week, I was trapped in a heavy traffic jam in front of the City College on Mirpur Road. I went to New Market to take a birthday cake for my younger sister. Her birthday was on that day. I had to stay there for about 3 hours. So, I felt very much embarrassed. There are many chances why traffic jams occur. Reckless driving, disobeying of traffic rules and overtaking other vehicles are some of the causes of traffic jam. In our daily life, traffic jam creates a lot of problems. People cannot go from one place to another easily. To get rid of this problem, we have to take some necessary steps. The roads should be widened. The drivers should obey traffic rules and should not overtake any vehicles. To lead the country to the path of development we should be careful to solve the problem of traffic jam.
question_text: Suppose, you experienced a traffic jam last week. Now, write a paragraph on "A Traffic Jam You Experienced". [CB '17]

answer_text:
A Book Fair
A book fair is of fairly a recent origin. It is a fair where different types of books are displayed for sale. Nowadays book fair has become very popular. A book fair is usually held in the months of January and February. In our country it is held in almost all cities and towns. The largest book fair is organized by Bangla Academy on the occasion of the 21st February. It is called the "Amar Ekushe Boi Mela". It has created a sense of interest for books amongst the general mass. In a book fair various types of pavillions are set up. Different sorts of books like fictions, text books, dramas, children books, reference books etc. are displayed catagorically. There are also snacks, food and drink stalls. A book fair becomes crowdy specially in the evening. Customers irrespective of age, gender, caste and creed gather at a book fair. Renowned and promising writers visit the fiar regularly. Seminars and cultural programmes are held. The main purpose of a book fair is not only sale but it offers a rare opportunity to assess the advancement made in publication of books. It helps to create new writers as well as new readers. It inspires all sections of people to form the habit of reading. A book fair bears the testimony of the refined tastes and varied culture of a country. A book fair reminds us that books change our outlook on life and widens our domain of knowledge. Readers get these best friends at a cheaper rate from a book fair. Thus, book fairs are of great value as they help to build an enlightened society and nation.

answer_text:
A Moon-lit Night
A moonlit night is a night when the moon beams with its full size and gleam. Such a night looks very beautiful. The whole nature takes a heavenly look. People come out of homes so that they can enjoy the glamourous night, especially the cloudless one. People rush on the roads and open square to enjoy the beauties of nature. Some enjoy gossiping, some play pipes in the fields and some others sing songs. The children and women also come out to watch the moon-lit night. They become excited and amazed to watch the beauty of nature. The poets write poems about the moon-lit night. They describe it with their imagination. Even common people try to compose poems in such a splendid situation. A moon-lit night reminds us of the renowned song of Rabindranath Tagore "Chander Hashi Bandh Bhengeche." I have a memory of experiencing a moonlit night at our village home when I went there during my summer vacation. On that night, the moon was beaming lavishly. The brightness of the moon's light was so heavy that it looked like almost day light. To see that brilliance of the moon's light, our joys knew no bound. Infact, a moonlit night is a blessing of the Almighty to all his dearly creatures.

question_text: Write a paragraph on "A Moon-lit Night". [Combined Board Exam '18]

answer_text:
The Life of a Rickshaw Puller
A rickshaw puller is one who pulls rickshaw to take passengers to their destinations (গন্তব্য). He is a poor day labourer. In fact, finding no other means a man pulls rickshaw to earn his livelihood. Most often a rickshaw puller does not have his own rickshaw. He hires a rickshaw from a rickshaw owner on daily basis. Pulling a rickshaw is no doubt, a toilsome work. Even he has to pull rickshaw in rain or sun. Because, if he stops pulling rickshaw someday, he along with his family has to starve. A rickshaw puller pulls his rickshaw from dawn to dusk. Even if he feels out of sorts, he has to come out with his rickshaw to earn his livelihood. Moreover, sometimes he receives misbehaviour (দুর্ব্যবহার) from the passengers. Usually a rickshaw puller earns tk. 200 to 300 a day from which he has to pay the rent of the rickshaw to the rickshaw owner. If he earns too little someday for some reasons, he doesn't have anything left after paying the rent of the rickshaw. If his rickshaw breaks down for having an accident on roads, his miseries are beyond description. We should behave with him nicely. On a whole, a rickshaw puller leads his daily life in great difficulty.
flag_note: ছাপা নম্বরের প্রথম অঙ্ক পৃষ্ঠার কিনারায় কাটা — শুধু '2.' দেখা যায়; নম্বর 22 ধারাবাহিকতা থেকে ধরা হয়েছে।
question_text: A rickshaw puller is a very familiar figure in our country. He plays a great role in our communication system. But he leads a very miserable life for financial problem. Now, write a paragraph in 150 words on "The life of a rickshaw puller". [DB '17]

answer_text:
The Benefits of Early Rising
'Early rising' means to get up from bed early in the morning. If one wishes to rise early in the morning, he can make it into a habit. At first he may not be habituated to rise early in the morning. But after rising for some days, he may build such a habit that will encourage him to rise early in the morning spontaneously. So, a time obviously comes when he can't but rise early in the morning. An early riser can be beneficial in various ways. He can enjoy the fresh air of the morning and be mentally refreshed. Walking in the morning builds up his body. He can start his daily work early in the morning. A person who does not rise early in the morning generally faces some problems. He often gets up late and gets late for his office. He can't enjoy the fresh air of the morning. He can't take a walk in the morning which can benefit him physically. On the other hand, an early riser benefits the society in various ways. As he possesses a good health, he may contribute to the country largely. Being a punctual person, he may perform his duties timely. There is an English proverb "Early to bed, early to rise, makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise."
flag_note: ছাপা নম্বরের প্রথম অঙ্ক পৃষ্ঠার কিনারায় কাটা — শুধু '3.' দেখা যায়; নম্বর 23 ধারাবাহিকতা থেকে ধরা হয়েছে।
question_text: Early rising is a very good habit. It has many benefits for our happy and healthy life. Now, write a paragraph in 250 words on "The benefits of early rising". [CtgB '17]

answer_text:
Load-shedding
Load-shedding has become a hard nut to crack (কঠিন সমস্যা- gordian knot) in Bangladesh particularly in the urban areas where people largely depend on electricity. It means the discontinuation (ব্যাঘাত) of supply of electricity. It occurs while generation of power falls short of demand. Due to rapid growth of population the demand of electricity has increased to a great extent while the generation of power has not risen expectedly. It mostly occurs in the pick hour of the day that refers to the time from 8 am to 11 pm. When load shedding occurs, the normal life of the people of that area comes to a standstill. It creates the problem of far reaching consequences in the socio-economic (আর্থ-সামাজিক) development of the country. Mills and factories, shops, hospitals come to a standstill. Housewives, students, patients and workers also fall a victim to it. All the electronic devices like refrigerators, televisions, air conditioners, electric fans, computers, diagnostic devices in the hospitals become useless. We are also suffering a lot in our locality due to load-shedding. To get rid of this worst suffering, power generation should be increased. We should also (মিতব্যয়ী) be frugal in using electricity.
flag_note: ছাপা নম্বরের প্রথম অঙ্ক পৃষ্ঠার কিনারায় কাটা — শুধু '4.' দেখা যায়; নম্বর 24 ধারাবাহিকতা থেকে ধরা হয়েছে।
question_text: Suppose, you are in a great trouble for load-shedding in your locality. Now, write a paragraph on 'Load-shedding' in 150 words. [SB '17; DjB '16]

answer_text:
A Day Labourer
A fellow working on 'no work no pay' basis is normally a day labourer. He is not salaried though not honorary as well. He usually does the work of a farmer massively. He sometimes is engaged in masonry. He becomes a rickshaw puller, a railway porter and a temporary hawker to some extent. He generally has no fixed job. Now he is a stone breaker and then a soil cutter. In the markets of city areas some minor boys keep a basket with them and help the buyers carry their heavy load of shopping to their residence (বাসস্থান). They are also day labourers leading a miserable condition. In our country, a day labourer is not well paid. He works from sunrise to sunset and even late night. But he does not get expected remuneration (পারিশ্রমিক) from their owners. He is sun burnt with a mirth of having due wages. He is drenched with torrents like a storm crow. He shivers in the pinching cold to drag his hard life forward. Of course his joys know no bounds when he earns more. Then he shops with his basket full and returns to his shabby cottage where his diseased wife and some naked or half naked children wait for having some food. But the case is reverse when he goes on without any work. He wears a gloomy (বিষণ্ণ) appearance visualising the famished (না খেয়ে থাকা) mouths of his family. Then he is between two fires what to do for his family members awaiting food with rictus. The rigorous condition of our day labourers ought to be upgraded with the all out effort of both Govt and commoners.
question_text: Write a paragraph in 250 words on "A Day Labourer". [BB '17]

answer_text:
Our School Library
The word library is taken from the Latin word 'libre' which means a book. So we can say that a library is nothing but a collection of books. A school library means a house in the school where books are kept for the students as well as teachers. Our school has a library which is very spacious (wek vj). It is furnished with all modern facilities. Here almirahs are arranged in rows and tables are placed in the middle. Books are arranged in Dewey decimal system. Books including textbook, reference book and literary works are available here. Our school library also provides facilities including newspaper reading, organising debate (বিতর্ক), etc. Students can prepare their lessons as well as can take notes in the library. Even they are allowed to borrow books from the library by showing their library cards. In our library there are computers with internet facilities so that students can update themselves with the rest of the world. A school library is a must for spreading knowledge. It displays the rich store of knowledge. With the help of a library students can gather knowledge for building their better future.
flag_note: ছাপায় যেমন আছে তেমনই রাখা হয়েছে: 'spacious'-এর পরের টীকা ছাপাতেই বিকৃত লাতিন অক্ষরে '(wek vj)' লেখা — অর্থ অনিশ্চিত, অনুমান করে সংশোধন করা হয়নি।
question_text: Imagine, you are the students of a renowned school of the city. You have a very big and resourceful library. You use it regularly in a certain manner and get much benefit. Now, write a paragraph on "Your School Library" within 150 words. [DjB '17]

answer_text:
Traffic Jam
Traffic jam means blockade of vehicles on roads and streets. It is a problem of urban areas. There are a number of reasons of traffic jam. Unlicensed and unauthorised rickshaws are the main causes of traffic jam. Violating (অমান্য করে) traffic rules and regulations, illegal parking of vehicles on roads also causes traffic jam. Again, narrow roads and frequent digging for development work, cause traffic jam. Building materials piled on roads cause traffic jam too. Whatever the causes of traffic jam may be, it is a great threat of urban people. In our daily activities, we cannot become fast and punctual because traffic jam kills our valuable time. Office going people, school going children and dying patients are also a victim to traffic jam. So, it is our bounden responsibility to solve this problem. But there is no fixed way to solve this problem. It requires united action to solve this problem. Shops and markets should be removed from the roadsides. In some places, government should build fly-over and people should be made aware of the traffic rules and regulations. We should not cross the roads in an indisciplined (বিশৃঙ্খল) way. All these measures will help us to remove the traffic jam.
question_text: Traffic jam has become a very common phenomenon in big cities of Bangladesh. Suppose, you have got stuck in a long traffic jam on the way to examination hall. Now, write a paragraph in 250 words on "Traffic Jam". [CtgB '19]

answer_text:
The uses and abuses of Mobile Phone
Mobile phone refers to a telephone that does not have wires. It works by radio. One can carry it with oneself and use it anywhere. It is a recent scientific invention. It has created coruscation (আলোড়ন) all over the world. It is of great use to us. Besides communication with the people in distant places one can send message, know time-table, do calculation, play games and sports, hear songs and music, take snaps, be familiar with global culture by browsing internet with the help of mobile phone. And so its popularity is increasing day by day. One can communicate with one's near and dear persons in distant place in the twinkling of an eye by using mobile phone. It saves one's valuable time, energy and also money. One need not go to distant places to meet one's favourite persons for the use of mobile phone. With its golden touch, the countries of the world are like families in a village. But the mobile phone has still some drawbacks (খারাপ দিক) in disguise. Though its price is gradually decreasing per minute bill is not lessening. And so all cannot buy it. Scientists have recently discovered that mobile phone can cause cancer to the users. Besides, those who are terrorists use it at random and commit terrorist activities at large. Nevertheless, the importance of mobile phone in quick communication is very great.
question_text: Mobile phone is a part and parcel of our daily life. Now, write a paragraph in 250 words on "The uses and abuses of Mobile Phone". [BB '16]

answer_text:
A Rainy Day
A rainy day is a day when it rains a lot. During the day, the sky remains cloudy. A flash of lightning and a noise of thunder are seen and heard together. Sometimes heavy wind also blows during the day. On such a day, the day labourers cannot work, officials can not go to office. But the school goers get a golden opportunity having a rainy day. During a rainy day, they feel very happy as they do not need to go to school. They pass the day by playing indoor games like hide and seek, ludo, chess, carom etc. In fact, the school goers wish the day very much. But the poor can not welcome the day. Because of the fact that they have to suffer a lot during the day. During a rainy day, they can not earn their bread and butter and so they have to starve. Even they can not stay in their dilapidated cottages well as rain water enters into their living places. In fact, the poor have to pass a very miserable life during a rainy day.
question_text: Suppose, once on a rainy day you got drenched in rain water. Write a paragraph in 250 words on 'A Rainy Day'. [JB '15]

answer_text:
Smart Phone
A smart phone is a mobile or cellular phone that runs off a mobile operating system (OS) and functions like a mini computer. Smart phones also function as portable media players, digital cameras, video cameras and GPS navigational devices. Smart phone have become an essential part of our daily lives, offering a range of uses that have made communication, entertainment, and information sharing easier and more accessible. They have become a popular tool for connecting with friends and family, making calls, sending texts, taking online classes and using social media platforms. In addition to communication, smart phones have many other uses, including accessing the internet, taking photos and videos, playing games, and managing calendars and to-do lists. They also serve as a portable device for listening to music, watching movies and TV shows, and reading books. On the other hand, the misuse of mobile phones can lead to various negative consequences. One of the most significant abuses is addiction, which can interfere with personal relationships and daily routines. Overuse of smart phones can also lead to a sedentary lifestyle, leading to health issues such as obesity, eye strain, and neck and back pain. Another significant abuse is the use of smart phones while driving, which can cause accidents and fatalities. Cyber bullying is another form of smart phones abuse, which can lead to mental and emotional distress for the victim. Therefore, it is important to recognize the potential for misuse and to use them responsibly to avoid negative consequences. However, it is necessary to find a balance between the benefits and the drawbacks of smartphone usage, keeping in mind the safety and well-being of oneself and others.
question_text: Write a paragraph "Smart Phone" within 250 words. [JB '24]

answer_text:
Importance of Learning Computer
Importance of Learning computer is very important in today's digital age for various reasons. Firstly, computers are essential for modern communication, information processing, and problem-solving. They facilitate efficient data management and analysis enabling individuals and organizations to make informed decisions. Secondly, computers are utilized in various sectors such as education, healthcare, finance, entertainment, and manufacturing. From classrooms to hospitals to offices, computers are omnipresent, streaming processes and enhancing productivity. Additionally, computers can perform a wide range of tasks, including word processing, graphic design, programming, simulations, and data processing. Thus, they are versatile tools with applications across diverse fields. Many professions including software development, data analysis, cyber security, digital marketing and graphic design require proficiency in computer skills. Moreover, in today's technology-driven job market, basic computer literacy is prerequisite for almost every job. Therefore, students need to learn computer skills to prepare for future careers and to adapt to the evolving demands of the workforce. Overall, mastering computer skills equips individuals with the competencies necessary to thrive in the digital era.
question_text: Write a paragraph about "The Importance of Learning Computer". [BB '24]

answer_text:
Our School Magazine
A school magazine is generally a literary journal of the school. It is generally published annually or bi-annually. It is considered a training medium of literary writings by the young writers. We have a school magazine of our own. The name of our school magazine is 'Dishari'. It usually contains stories, poems, jokes, essays etc. To publish the magazine, a magazine committee is formed by the Principal. A senior teacher is selected as the editor and a student of the top class is selected as assistant editor. The topics for the magazine are selected by the editor who gives direction (wbG Ækbv) to the students to write properly. Among the writings, the authorities in charge select the writings to publish. They give priority for the creative writings. The school authority bears the expenditure (LiP/eÅq) of the magazine. The school magazine plays an important role in helping the students to express their feelings and thoughts. It is also helpful for the teachers to know the inner strength of their students. In fact, the school magazine is the perfect platform for the future writers. This literary magazine acts as a link between the ex-students and the present students of a school.
